name: Charred Pepper Sauce
intro: One jar. A week of flavor.
card_uses: Spoon it over a rice bowl.
method: Set a dry cast-iron pan over high heat until smoking. Add the peppers and jalapeños whole, and the garlic clove. Leave them alone — dark spots are the point. Turn occasionally until charred on most sides, about 12–15 minutes. Transfer peppers and jalapeños to a bowl, cover tight, and leave to steam for 15 minutes. Peel off skins and discard seeds. Squeeze the garlic from its skin. Blend everything with olive oil, sherry vinegar, and salt — leave a little texture rather than making it perfectly smooth. Taste and adjust.

storage.note: Keeps in the refrigerator for up to a week. The flavor deepens overnight.

uses.label: Rice bowl
uses.context: A generous spoonful on top. Let it pool slightly rather than mixing it in.

uses.label: Chicken thighs
uses.context: Spoon it next to the chicken rather than over it. Let the diner decide how much.

uses.label: Eggs
uses.context: Add a spoonful to scrambled eggs in the last 30 seconds. Or spoon it over fried eggs.

uses.label: Pasta
uses.context: Stir in a little olive oil or pasta water. Toss with warm pasta off the heat.

uses.label: White beans
uses.context: Spoon over beans and give them a few minutes. They absorb it slowly.
